title: Ambient-pressure room-temperature superconductivity in a manufacturable solid

concept.text: The innovation would be a bulk solid that reproducibly carries electrical current without resistance near room temperature at about one atmosphere, shows a bulk superconducting magnetic response, and retains those properties outside a pressure cell. It would also need to be processable into useful conductor. Discovering a superconducting transition in a microscopic sample would establish part of the physics; producing a stable material that can be made into wire, tape or another practical conductor would complete the technological ambition.

The supplied evidence illustrates two routes toward this goal: hydrogen-rich materials with very high transition temperatures under extreme pressure, and pressure quenching, which attempts to retain a pressure-induced or pressure-enhanced superconducting state after pressure is released. Neither route, in the results described here, establishes the full combination of room-temperature operation, atmospheric pressure, bulk stability and conductor manufacture.

significance.text: As a conditional consequence of the proposed capability, a useful conductor operating within its superconducting temperature, current and magnetic-field limits could eliminate DC resistive heating along its superconducting portion and avoid cryogenic refrigeration. Combining those properties with atmospheric-pressure operation would remove major constraints on where superconductors can be deployed. The revolutionary advance would therefore be a practical materials capability, with potential consequences for power delivery, motors and magnets.

Engineering synthesis: zero conductor resistance would not make an entire transmission system lossless. Joints, contacts, protection equipment and AC losses would still matter. Likewise, room-temperature superconductivity alone would not establish compact high-field magnets: those require sufficient current capacity in strong magnetic fields, mechanical strength and a workable device design. The reported suppression of the LaH10 transition by an external field illustrates why transition temperature and magnetic-field performance must be assessed separately.

Fusion systems, quantum electronics and other new devices are downstream possibilities rather than automatic consequences. The Hg-1223 paper discusses fusion and quantum technologies as potential applications, but does not demonstrate them. Grid redesign and new motor or magnet architectures would similarly require further materials and system engineering. No numerical estimate of worldwide electricity savings is justified by the supplied evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is to combine a high superconducting transition temperature with a material phase that survives at atmospheric pressure and remains usable near room temperature. The documented hydride result around 250 K requires about 170 GPa. Pressure-quenched Hg-1223 demonstrates retention of an enhanced superconducting state at atmospheric pressure, but its reported transition temperature is substantially lower and its retained state has limited thermal and temporal stability. These are distinct barriers: raising the transition temperature does not by itself solve pressure dependence or phase stability.

Synthesis must reproducibly produce the intended composition and structure, and measurements must establish superconductivity throughout a meaningful fraction of the material. A resistance onset alone does not establish a bulk superconducting state. Transport measurements and magnetic evidence answer complementary questions, so a convincing material would need both. The disagreement surrounding La-Sc-H also makes precursor choice, synthesis conditions and phase identification concrete issues: unsuccessful preparation of a different product cannot settle the properties of the claimed phase.

Engineering synthesis: the manufacturing barrier extends beyond making a larger specimen. Processing must preserve the superconducting phase and produce continuous conductor with useful current capacity, field tolerance, mechanical integrity and stable performance over time. A material that requires continuous extreme pressure, degrades during ordinary thermal handling, or loses its useful properties when formed into conductor would leave the titled innovation incomplete. These requirements describe the proposed technological target; the supplied results do not establish that they have been met.

current_state.text: Drozdov and colleagues reported superconductivity around 250 K at about 170 GPa in LaH10 in Nature 569, 528–531, published on 22 May 2019. The abstract identifies zero resistance, an isotope effect and suppression of the transition temperature by an external magnetic field as experimental evidence. This is a dated high-pressure achievement, not an exclusive present-day ceiling on hydride transition temperatures or a demonstration at atmospheric pressure. The supplied review had access to subscription-preview material, including the abstract, rather than the full paper.

Two papers associated with Ranga Dias were subsequently retracted, but they concerned different pressure regimes. The carbonaceous sulfur hydride room-temperature superconductivity paper was retracted on 26 September 2022 over susceptibility-data processing concerns; the notice records author disagreement. The nitrogen-doped lutetium hydride near-ambient superconductivity paper was retracted on 7 November 2023. That notice describes concerns about material provenance, experimental measurements and data-processing protocols, together with credible unresolved concerns about resistance data. These papers cannot serve as established demonstrations of the proposed capability.

Deng and colleagues reported pressure-quenched Hg-1223 in PNAS 123, e2536178123, in March 2026. They reported ambient-pressure resistive onset temperatures up to 151 K. A retrieved sample showed a reported bulk magnetic response at approximately 140 K. The maximum resistive onset and the magnetic result on the extracted sample are separate observations and should not be combined into a claim of bulk magnetic confirmation at 151 K.

The retained Hg-1223 phase was reported stable for at least three days when stored in liquid nitrogen at 77 K, while its transition temperature degraded after heating above 200 K. This establishes an important pressure-release result within a restricted stability window, rather than a material stable during room-temperature use. Although the earlier research notes could not reopen a separate publisher PDF, the supplied review had full main-article XML text supporting this stability statement. Figures and separate supplementary material were not inspected in that review.

Song and colleagues' arXiv preprint, submitted on 29 September 2025 and revised on 6 October 2025, reports superconducting onset temperatures of 271–298 K at 195–266 GPa in a La-Sc-H phase assigned to LaSc2H24. These are reported near-room-temperature onsets under extreme pressure in a diamond-anvil experiment. They do not demonstrate atmospheric-pressure operation or a manufacturable conductor. The supplied review supports attribution of the reported ranges, but does not establish independent confirmation or subsequent journal-publication status. Its paper extraction had recorded parsing issues and was treated as partial; figures were not visually inspected, and no demonstrated Meissner result is inferred.

Semenok and colleagues' arXiv preprint, submitted on 28 May 2026 and revised on 20 August 2026, reports seven synthesis attempts with no superconductivity detected at 245–300 K in the resulting hydrides. This is evidence of unresolved reproducibility, rather than definitive disproof of Song's result. Their discussion identifies precursor choice and synthesis limitations as potentially important, so the attempts do not establish that an independently verified identical phase lacks the claimed properties. The supplied review had the paper text, but did not visually inspect its figures.

The research notes also identify a July 2026 single-group report of transitions up to 187 K in boron-doped Q-carbon. No text or other retained artifact for that citation was available to the supplied review, so its measurements, interpretation and reproducibility cannot be assessed here. That evidence gap is not proof that the reported result is false.

An Argonne Advanced Photon Source highlight dated 4 November 2026 describes the Hg-1223 pressure-quench result and characterizes the preceding ambient-pressure transition-temperature benchmark as 133 K. It followed the March PNAS publication; it did not precede the underlying result. It also falls after the supplied review's 1 November 2026 cutoff and therefore cannot establish what was known by that cutoff. Its omission of Q-carbon does not demonstrate rejection of that report or a community consensus about it.

Scope of this account: the supplied results do not demonstrate a stable, manufacturable atmospheric-pressure room-temperature conductor. They document substantial advances in temperature under pressure and in retaining enhanced superconductivity after pressure release, alongside unresolved stability and reproducibility questions. Because no bounded freshness search record was supplied, this account does not certify an exhaustive inventory of materials or establish an exclusive current record.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed scientific demonstration, not an established standard: independent laboratories would reproduce zero resistance and a Meissner response at a specified room-temperature operating point, at approximately one atmosphere and outside a pressure cell. The superconducting volume fraction should be quantified, with sufficient sample volume for ordinary magnetometry. Measurements should identify the material phase and establish that electrical and magnetic observations concern the same reproducibly prepared material.
completion_criteria.label: Labs reproduce room-temperature zero resistance and Meissner response at one atmosphere

completion_criteria.text: Proposed intermediate milestone: the same combination of transport and magnetic evidence near or above 273 K would be valuable, but operation near the ice point would not by itself establish the room-temperature target. The final demonstration should explicitly state its operating temperature and pressure rather than rely on an ambiguous description of ambient conditions. A microscopic transition onset measured only inside a pressure cell would not meet the proposed bulk atmospheric-pressure criterion.
completion_criteria.label: Bulk atmospheric-pressure evidence with operating temperature and pressure stated

completion_criteria.text: Proposed current-carrying demonstration: a closed loop made from the material would sustain persistent current under the claimed temperature and pressure conditions, with measurement duration, detection limits and current magnitude reported. This would provide a further functional milestone, but would not alone establish scalable conductor manufacture or useful current capacity in strong magnetic fields.
completion_criteria.label: Closed loop sustains persistent current with measurement limits reported

completion_criteria.text: Proposed technological completion: reproducible batches would be manufactured into long conductor, with specified current capacity, magnetic-field tolerance, mechanical handling limits and stability during storage and operation. Practical evaluation should include thermal cycling, joints and any application-relevant AC behavior. Independent reproduction should cover both synthesis and conductor performance. Such finite demonstrations would establish breadth over the tested lengths, batches, durations and operating conditions; they would not prove unlimited durability or performance under every condition.
completion_criteria.label: Independently reproduced long conductors meet specified performance and stability limits

related_concepts.text: MAS-02, Bulk structural solids that are both near their ideal strength and damage-tolerant: mechanical strength and resistance to damage could help superconducting conductors survive manufacture and magnet forces. MAS-01 centers on superconducting electrical and magnetic behavior; exceptional structural strength would neither establish superconductivity nor be required at the ideal-strength level for every application. This is a conceptual relationship inferred from the supplied roster.

MAS-03, General atomically precise covalent construction: control over atomic composition and structure could assist preparation of candidate superconducting phases. General covalent construction is a broader fabrication capability, while MAS-01 could potentially be achieved through a narrower synthesis route without general atomic precision. This is a conceptual relationship inferred from the supplied roster.

MAS-04, A reliable map from a property specification to a makeable material: such a discovery capability could help find materials combining high transition temperature, atmospheric-pressure stability and processability. MAS-01 asks for a particular material capability; MAS-04 asks for a general way to move from desired properties to materials that can actually be made. This is a conceptual relationship inferred from the supplied roster.

MAS-05, Structural solids that remain engineering materials after fusion-level atomic displacement: both innovations could contribute to fusion systems, through different roles. MAS-01 could support superconducting magnets if its field and current performance were adequate; MAS-05 concerns structural survival under radiation damage. A superconducting magnet material would not automatically meet the structural radiation-tolerance target. This is a conceptual relationship inferred from the supplied roster.

MAS-06, Reversible solids that store energy at chemical-fuel specific energy: superconductivity could enable persistent-current energy storage, but zero resistance alone does not establish chemical-fuel-level specific energy. The storage target depends on achievable energy per mass and practical containment, whereas MAS-01 concerns the conductor's operating state and manufacturability. This is a conceptual relationship inferred from the supplied roster.

MAS-07, Programmable growth of load-bearing solids: controlled growth might offer ways to form or integrate superconducting material, but programmable structural growth and superconducting performance are separate capabilities. MAS-01 does not require a general ability to grow load-bearing structures. This is a conceptual relationship inferred from the supplied roster.

MAS-08, An ambient catalytic solid that fixes nitrogen at industrial intensity: both concepts seek useful solid-state functionality under ordinary pressure rather than demanding operating conditions. Their scientific targets differ: MAS-08 concerns catalytic reaction rates and nitrogen conversion, while MAS-01 concerns superconducting transport and magnetic behavior. Success in either would not establish the other. This is a conceptual relationship inferred from the supplied roster.

MAS-09, Structural metals that fully recover from macroscopic fracture in service: repair capability could improve conductor durability, but recovery from fracture would also need to restore electrical continuity and superconducting performance to benefit MAS-01. A stable superconducting conductor need not be self-healing, and a self-healing structural metal need not be superconducting. This is a conceptual relationship inferred from the supplied roster.

MAS-10, Topologically protected quantum matter outside the dilution refrigerator: both concern useful quantum behavior at less demanding temperatures. Ordinary superconductivity does not by itself establish topological protection or robust quantum-information functionality, and operation outside a dilution refrigerator need not mean room-temperature operation. The entries therefore retain distinct physical and technological completion criteria. This is a conceptual relationship inferred from the supplied roster.

change_log.change: Preserved MAS-01 and its title while defining separate scientific and manufacturing requirements.
change_log.reason: Bulk superconductivity, atmospheric-pressure retention and useful conductor manufacture are complementary parts of the original concept.

change_log.change: Replaced unrestricted claims about all known pairing states with statements bounded by the supplied demonstrated materials.
change_log.reason: The sources document important operating limits but do not establish an exhaustive inventory or exclusive current benchmark.

change_log.change: Qualified lossless transmission and compact high-field magnets, and retained fusion and electronics as conditional downstream possibilities.
change_log.reason: DC conductor resistance, AC losses, joints, field-dependent current capacity and mechanical performance are distinct engineering constraints.

change_log.change: Treated the 2019 LaH10 result as a dated achievement rather than a present-day hydride ceiling.
change_log.reason: The reported 250 K at about 170 GPa does not establish an exclusive temperature or pressure limit.

change_log.change: Distinguished the two retracted papers and their stated concerns.
change_log.reason: The carbonaceous sulfur hydride paper should not be grouped with the nitrogen-doped lutetium hydride paper as two near-ambient-pressure claims.

change_log.change: Separated Hg-1223's maximum 151 K resistive onset from the approximately 140 K magnetic response on a retrieved sample.
change_log.reason: Combining the observations would overstate magnetic confirmation at the maximum onset temperature.

change_log.change: Integrated Hg-1223's quantified stability window and corrected the PNAS/Argonne chronology.
change_log.reason: The supplied review retained full main-article XML supporting at least three days at 77 K and degradation above 200 K; the March paper preceded the November highlight.

change_log.change: Presented the La-Sc-H reports as an unresolved reproducibility question with synthesis-dependent qualifications.
change_log.reason: The reported high-pressure onsets are not independently established here, while unsuccessful synthesis attempts do not definitively refute an identical verified phase.

change_log.change: Retained the Q-carbon report with explicit evidence limits and removed the inference of community non-adoption.
change_log.reason: No retained source text was available, and Argonne's omission cannot establish rejection or consensus.

change_log.change: Recast 273 K and persistent-current tests as intermediate proposed milestones, then added room-temperature and conductor-performance demonstrations.
change_log.reason: Neither ice-point operation nor a persistent-current loop alone completes the titled innovation.

change_log.change: Added distinctions for every other supplied roster entry without merging concepts.
change_log.reason: Shared enabling methods or downstream applications do not make the underlying breakthroughs interchangeable.

change_log.change: Excluded the unrelated 2015 APS upgrade PDF from scientific support while retaining the valid 2026 highlight.
change_log.reason: The supplied review identified the PDF as a different document despite its association with the highlight in the source index.

unresolved_issues: No bounded freshness search record was supplied, so the account cannot certify exhaustive coverage as of 1 November 2026 or establish an exclusive current record.
The Argonne highlight is dated 4 November 2026, after the review cutoff. It is retained as explicitly later context rather than evidence of the earlier state of knowledge.
The Q-carbon report's measurements, superconducting interpretation and reproducibility remain unassessed because no source text was retained.

Independent reproducibility of the reported La-Sc-H high-temperature transitions remains unresolved, including whether unsuccessful syntheses produced the same phase under sufficiently comparable conditions.
The supplied record does not establish subsequent journal-publication status for either arXiv report.
The 2019 Nature paper was available only in preview; Song's extraction had recorded issues; relevant figures and Hg-1223 supplementary material were not inspected in the supplied review.
A specific room-temperature operating point, useful conductor length, current capacity, field range and acceptable service lifetime remain to be defined for a concrete completion program.
